vlc.name: VLC Media Player
general_tips: VLC preferences are split into 'Simple' and 'All' modes – many settings are only visible in 'All' mode.
To access advanced settings: Tools → Preferences, then click the 'All' radio button at the bottom left.
The VLC configuration file is located at ~/.config/vlc/vlcrc for fine‑tuned adjustments.
Press Space to toggle play/pause, F to toggle full screen and M to mute/unmute.
You can drag and drop media files directly into the player window to start playback.

steps: 1. Open VLC Media Player.
2. Go to Tools → Preferences (or press Ctrl+P).
3. IMPORTANT: Click the 'All' radio button at the bottom left to show all settings.
4. CRITICAL: In the left panel tree, use DOUBLE_CLICK on 'Interface' to expand it (single click only selects).
5. Use DOUBLE_CLICK on 'Main interfaces' to expand it.
6. LEFT_CLICK on 'Qt' under Main interfaces to select it.
7. In the right panel, uncheck 'Display background cone or art'.
8. Click Save and restart VLC.
1. Open VLC and go to Tools → Preferences.
2. Click 'All' to show advanced settings.
3. Navigate to Interface → Main interfaces → Qt.
4. Check 'Start in minimal view mode'.
5. Or use Ctrl+H to toggle minimal view.
1. Open VLC and go to Tools → Preferences.
2. Look for the 'Playlist and Instances' section.
3. Uncheck 'Use only one instance when started from file manager'.
4. Uncheck 'Allow only one instance'.
5. Click Save.
1. Play your video in VLC.
2. Click on Subtitle → Add Subtitle File…
3. Browse to the .srt or subtitle file and select it.
4. The subtitles will load automatically during playback.
1. Open your media in VLC.
2. Press '+' to increase speed or '-' to decrease speed.
3. Alternatively, go to Playback → Speed and choose Faster, Slower or Normal.
1. Pause the video at the frame you want to capture.
2. Go to Video → Take Snapshot or press Shift+S.
3. The snapshot will be saved to your pictures directory (check Preferences → Video for the exact path).
1. Start playing a media file in VLC.
2. Click the Loop button in the control bar or press L until the desired loop mode (repeat one or repeat all) is selected.
3. The playback will now repeat according to the chosen mode.
1. While watching a video or listening to audio, press Ctrl+Up Arrow to increase volume.
2. Press Ctrl+Down Arrow to decrease volume.
3. You can also use the mouse wheel over the volume slider in the player interface.
1. Open the video file in VLC.
2. Go to Tools → Effects and Filters.
3. In the Video Effects tab, open the Geometry sub‑tab.
4. Check 'Transform' and choose the rotation angle (e.g., Rotate by 90 degrees) from the drop‑down list.
5. Click Close to preview the rotated video.
6. To permanently save the rotated video, go to Media → Convert/Save, add the video, click Convert/Save, choose a profile and click Start; VLC will encode the rotated video to a new file.
1. Open VLC and go to Media → Convert/Save.
2. Click Add and select the video file whose audio you want to extract.
3. Click Convert/Save to open the conversion dialog.
4. Under Profile, choose 'Audio – MP3'.
5. Click Browse to choose a destination filename with .mp3 extension and click Save.
6. Click Start to begin the conversion; the resulting MP3 file will be saved at the chosen location.
1. Open VLC and go to View → Advanced Controls to reveal red record button.
2. Play the video and navigate to the starting point of the segment you want to keep.
3. Click the red record button to start recording.
4. Let the video play until it reaches the end of the desired segment, then click the record button again to stop.
5. The trimmed segment will be saved in your Videos folder (the exact location is shown in VLC’s message log).

libreoffice_writer.name: LibreOffice Writer
general_tips: Use the Format menu for text formatting operations.
Ctrl+S to save, Ctrl+Shift+S for Save As.
Export to PDF via File → Export As → Export as PDF.
Ctrl+B toggles bold; Ctrl+I toggles italic; Ctrl+U toggles underline.
Use the Styles and Formatting sidebar (F11) to apply consistent headings and paragraph styles.

steps: 1. Select the text you want to modify.
2. Go to Format → Character.
3. In the Font tab, select the desired font and size.
4. Click OK.
1. Select the text or heading.
2. Press Ctrl+E for center alignment.
3. Or go to Format → Align → Centered.
1. Highlight the text you want to embolden.
2. Press Ctrl+B or click the Bold icon on the toolbar.
3. Press Ctrl+B again to remove bold formatting.
1. Select the paragraph(s) whose spacing you want to change.
2. Go to Format → Paragraph.
3. In the Indents & Spacing tab, choose Single, 1.5 Lines, Double, or custom spacing from the Line Spacing dropdown.
4. Click OK.
1. Place the cursor where you want to create a list or select existing lines.
2. Click the Bullets and Numbering icon on the toolbar or go to Format → Bullets and Numbering.
3. Choose a bullet style and click OK.
1. Place the cursor at the insertion point in your document.
2. Go to Insert → Image.
3. Browse to the image file and click Open.
4. Resize or move the image as needed using the handles.
1. Go to Insert → Header and Footer.
2. Choose Default Style (or another page style) for Header or Footer.
3. A header/footer area appears where you can type your text (e.g., page numbers, document title).
1. Finish editing your document in Writer.
2. Go to File → Export As → Export as PDF.
3. Choose the export options (e.g., range, image resolution) and click Export.
4. Enter the file name and location, then click Save.
1. Select the text you want to convert to lowercase.
2. Go to Format → Text → Lowercase.
3. The selected text will change to all lowercase characters.
1. Select the comma‑separated values in your document.
2. Go to Table → Convert → Text to Table…
3. Under 'Separate text at', choose Commas (,).
4. Specify the number of columns if needed and click OK; the text will convert into a table.
1. Place the cursor at the end of a sentence.
2. Press Enter twice to create a blank line after the sentence.
3. Repeat for each sentence you need to separate.

4. Alternatively, use Find & Replace with a regular expression to automate: search for "." and replace with ".

" with Regular expressions enabled.
1. Place the cursor where you want to start a new page.
2. Go to Insert → Page Break or press Ctrl+Enter.
3. A blank page will be inserted after the current content.
1. Select the word list or text you want to color.
2. Use the toolbar’s Text Color dropdown to choose a color for vowels (e.g., red).
3. Manually highlight each word starting with a vowel and apply the chosen color.
4. Then choose another color (e.g., blue) for consonant‑starting words and apply it similarly.
5. You can use Find → Find & Replace with regular expressions to select words starting with vowels or consonants for faster formatting.

libreoffice_calc.name: LibreOffice Calc
general_tips: Use formulas starting with = to perform calculations.
Press Enter to confirm cell input.
Ctrl+Home jumps to cell A1; Ctrl+Arrow keys jump to the end of data ranges.
Use Data → Define Range to name ranges for easier formula references.
AutoSave can be configured under Tools → Options → Load/Save → General.

steps: 1. Click on the cell where you want the sum.
2. Type =SUM( and select the range of cells you want to add.
3. Close the parenthesis and press Enter.
1. Select the data range you want to sort (including the column headers, if present).
2. Go to Data → Sort.
3. Choose the column to sort by and select Ascending or Descending order.
4. Click OK to apply the sort.
1. Highlight the data range you want to visualize, including headers.
2. Click Insert → Chart or press F11.
3. Choose the chart type (e.g., line, bar, pie) and click Next.
4. Adjust the data series and labels if necessary, then click Finish to insert the chart.
1. Select the range or table you want to filter.
2. Go to Data → AutoFilter.
3. Drop‑down arrows appear on your column headers; click an arrow and choose criteria to filter rows.
4. Clear the filter via Data → AutoFilter again.
1. Click in the row below the row you want to freeze (e.g., click A2 to freeze the first row).
2. Go to View → Freeze Rows and Columns → Freeze First Row.
3. A thick line will appear indicating the frozen row.
4. To unfreeze, return to View → Freeze Rows and Columns and deselect the option.
1. Select the cell where you want the result to appear.
2. Type '=' followed by your formula (e.g., =A2*B2 for multiplication, =AVERAGE(A1:A10) for an average).
3. Press Enter to calculate the result.
4. Use the formula bar to edit complex formulas.
1. Select the range of numbers you want to change or press Ctrl+A to select the entire sheet.
2. Go to Format → Cells… and open the Numbers tab.
3. Choose a Number category (e.g., Number) and click the 'Format' field.
4. In the Format Code box, replace the period (.) decimal separator with a comma (,), such as #,##0.00 → #,##0,00.
5. Click OK to apply; numbers will display with commas as decimal separators.
1. Suppose the original numbers are in column A (Old ID). Select the cell in the new column (e.g., B2).
2. Enter the formula =TEXT(A2;"0000000") and press Enter; this pads the number with leading zeros to 7 digits.
3. Drag the fill handle down to apply the formula to the rest of the column.
4. Copy and Paste Special → Values if you need to convert formulas to static text.
1. If the birthdates are in column B, select the cell where you want to display the age (e.g., C2).
2. Enter the formula =INT((TODAY()-B2)/365.25) to approximate the age in years.
3. Press Enter and copy the formula down the column for other rows.
4. Alternatively, use =DATEDIF(B2;TODAY();"Y") for an exact whole number of years.
1. Select the column containing names or values with duplicates.
2. Copy the column to a new location where you want the unique list.
3. With the copied range selected, go to Data → More Filters → Standard Filter.
4. Choose 'No duplication' under Options and click OK; only unique entries remain.
5. Alternatively, use the function =UNIQUE(A1:A100) if your LibreOffice version supports it.
1. Select the data range you want to analyze (including column headers).
2. Go to Insert → Pivot Table… and choose 'Current selection'.
3. In the Pivot Table Layout dialog, drag the field (e.g., Invoice Number) to the Row Fields area and drag the same field to the Data Fields area with the function 'Count'.
4. Click OK; a new sheet appears with the pivot table summarizing counts per invoice number.

chrome.name: Google Chrome / Chromium
general_tips: Settings are accessed via the three‑dot menu → Settings.
chrome://extensions manages installed extensions.
Ctrl+Shift+N opens a new Incognito window.
Ctrl+L focuses the address bar; you can quickly type a URL or search query.
Use Bookmark bar (Ctrl+Shift+B) to toggle its visibility.

steps: 1. Open Chrome and go to Settings via the three‑dot menu.
2. Click on 'Search engine' in the sidebar.
3. Click 'Manage search engines and site search'.
4. Find your desired search engine in the list and click the three dots next to it.
5. Select 'Make default'.
1. Press Ctrl+Shift+Delete or go to Settings → Privacy and security → Clear browsing data.
2. Choose the time range (e.g., Last hour, Last 24 hours, All time).
3. Select which data to remove (Browsing history, Cookies, Cached images/files).
4. Click Clear data.
1. Press Ctrl+Shift+N to open a new Incognito window.
2. Alternatively, click the three‑dot menu and choose 'New Incognito window'.
3. Incognito mode will not save browsing history or cookies.
1. While on the page you want to bookmark, press Ctrl+D or click the star icon in the address bar.
2. Choose a folder or create a new one for the bookmark.
3. Rename the bookmark if desired and click Done.
1. Go to Settings → On startup.
2. Select 'Open a specific page or set of pages'.
3. Click 'Add a new page' and enter the desired homepage URL.
4. Click Add to save the homepage.
1. Open Settings → Privacy and security → Site settings.
2. Under 'Permissions', click Notifications.
3. Toggle 'Sites can ask to send notifications' off, or manage the block/allow lists for specific sites.
1. Perform a Google search or go to google.com and sign in if necessary.
2. Click the Settings gear icon below the search bar and choose 'Search settings'.
3. Under 'Results per page', move the slider to the desired number (e.g., 50).
4. Scroll down and click Save; confirm if prompted.
5. Your search results pages will now show the specified number of results.
1. Open the website you want to create a shortcut for.
2. Click the three‑dot menu → More tools → Create shortcut…
3. Optionally rename the shortcut and choose 'Open as window' if you want it to behave like an app.
4. Click Create; a desktop icon will appear that opens the site in Chrome.
1. Unzip or extract the extension folder if it is in a .zip file.
2. Go to chrome://extensions in the address bar.
3. Toggle Developer mode on (switch in the top right).
4. Click 'Load unpacked' and browse to the extension’s extracted folder.
5. Select the folder and click Open; the extension will load and appear in your extensions list.
1. Open Settings → Privacy and security → Site settings.
2. Click 'View permissions and data stored across sites' or 'All sites'.
3. Scroll to or search for the domain (e.g., amazon.com) and click the arrow.
4. Click 'Clear data' or 'Delete' to remove cookies and site data for that specific site.
5. Confirm the deletion when prompted.
1. Obtain the .crx or .zip extension file on your computer.
2. Navigate to chrome://extensions and enable Developer mode.
3. Drag and drop the .crx file onto the extensions page or click 'Load unpacked' and select the extracted folder if zipped.
4. Confirm installation when Chrome prompts you.
5. The extension will be added to your browser.

gimp.name: GNU Image Manipulation Program
general_tips: The Colors menu contains brightness, contrast and saturation adjustments.
Use File → Export As to save in different formats (PNG, JPEG, etc.).
Layers are essential for non‑destructive editing; use the Layers panel to add, hide or reorder layers.
Right‑clicking on an image opens a context menu with many operations for the selected tool.
Use Ctrl+Z to undo and Ctrl+Shift+Z to redo edits.

steps: 1. Open an image in GIMP.
2. Go to Colors → Brightness‑Contrast.
3. Adjust the Brightness and Contrast sliders to your liking.
4. Click OK to apply the changes.
1. Select the Crop Tool from the toolbox (or press Shift+C).
2. Click and drag to draw a rectangle over the area you want to keep.
3. Press Enter to crop the image to the selected region.
1. Go to Image → Scale Image…
2. Enter the new Width and Height values (maintain aspect ratio by clicking the chain icon).
3. Choose an interpolation method (e.g., Cubic) and click Scale.
1. Go to Image → Transform → Rotate 90° clockwise/counter‑clockwise or 180°.
2. Alternatively, choose Tools → Transform Tools → Rotate for a free rotation and enter a specific angle.
3. Click Rotate to apply the rotation.
1. Select the Text Tool from the toolbox (the large 'A' icon) or press T.
2. Click on the image where you want to add text and draw a text box.
3. Type your text and adjust font, size, and color from the Tool Options dock.
4. Use the Move Tool to reposition the text layer if needed.
1. Ensure the layer you want to blur is selected in the Layers panel.
2. Go to Filters → Blur → Gaussian Blur…
3. Adjust the Horizontal and Vertical blur radius values to control the intensity.
4. Click OK to apply the blur.
1. Open the video file in GIMP as an image sequence (File → Open as Layers and select the video; GIMP will import frames).
2. In the Layers panel, select and delete frames outside of your desired range (e.g., delete frames before the 2nd second and after the 4th second).
3. To export the trimmed segment as a video or animated GIF, go to File → Export As and choose an appropriate format (e.g., GIF for animations).
4. Set animation parameters (frame delay) if exporting as GIF and click Export.
1. Open your image in GIMP.
2. Go to Image → Mode → Grayscale.
3. The image will convert to shades of gray; you can undo (Ctrl+Z) to revert.
4. Save or export the grayscale image as needed.
1. Open the image and add an Alpha Channel via Layer → Transparency → Add Alpha Channel.
2. Use the Fuzzy Select Tool or Select by Color Tool to select the background area.
3. Press Delete to remove the selected background; transparent checkerboard appears.
4. Use Eraser or refine selection if needed and export as PNG to preserve transparency.
1. Prepare each frame of your animation as a separate layer (File → Open as Layers for multiple images).
2. Ensure layers are in the correct order from bottom (first frame) to top (last frame).
3. Go to File → Export As and choose a .gif file extension.
4. In the Export dialog, check 'As animation' and set frame delay and looping options.
5. Click Export to generate the animated GIF.

vscode.name: Visual Studio Code
general_tips: Press Ctrl+Shift+P to open the Command Palette for quick commands.
Type '>' in the Command Palette for built‑in commands or '@' to search symbols in the current file.
Ctrl+, opens the Settings UI; you can search settings by keyword.
Ctrl+` opens an integrated terminal; use multiple terminals via the dropdown next to the plus icon.
Use workspaces (File → Add Folder to Workspace) to manage multiple project folders.

steps: 1. Open VS Code.
2. Press Ctrl+Shift+P to open the Command Palette.
3. Type 'Preferences: Open Settings (UI)' and press Enter.
4. Use the search bar in the Settings UI to find the setting you want to change and modify it.
1. Press Ctrl+Shift+X to open the Extensions view.
2. In the search box, type the name or keywords of the extension you want.
3. Click Install next to the extension in the results list.
4. Once installed, you may need to reload VS Code to activate it.
1. Press Ctrl+K followed by Ctrl+T to open the theme picker.
2. Scroll through the list and select a color theme you like.
3. The theme changes immediately; you can preview and select as needed.
1. Press Ctrl+Shift+F to open the Search view.
2. Enter the text you want to find across your project.
3. Click the Enter key; results appear in the panel.
4. Click a result to open the file at the matching line.
1. Place the cursor on the line you want to comment.
2. Press Ctrl+/ to toggle a single‑line comment.
3. Select multiple lines and press Ctrl+/ to comment or uncomment them.
4. For block comments in some languages (e.g., HTML, CSS), press Shift+Alt+A.
1. Open the file you want to format.
2. Press Shift+Alt+F to format the document according to the default or selected formatter.
3. Ensure you have a formatter extension installed (e.g., Prettier, Black).
1. Open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P).
2. Type 'Preferences: Open Keyboard Shortcuts (JSON)' and press Enter to open keybindings.json.
3. Add a rule object with the command to remove, prefixed with a minus sign; for example: { "key": "ctrl+f", "command": "-list.find" } to unassign Ctrl+F from the Tree view find command.
4. Save the file; the keybinding is removed.
1. Open Settings (Ctrl+,).
2. In the search box, type 'files.exclude'.
3. Click 'Edit in settings.json' to open settings.json for modifications.
4. Add an entry under "files.exclude": "**/__pycache__": true and save the file.
5. __pycache__ directories will now be hidden from the Explorer.
1. Open Settings (Ctrl+,).
2. Search for 'auto save' in the settings search bar.
3. Change 'Files: Auto Save' to 'afterDelay'.
4. Set 'Files: Auto Save Delay' to the desired milliseconds (e.g., 500).
5. Files will auto save after the specified delay.
1. Click File → Open Folder… (or press Ctrl+K then Ctrl+O).
2. Browse to the project directory you want to open and click Select Folder.
3. VS Code loads the folder and displays its contents in the Explorer pane.
1. Press Ctrl+H to open the Replace tab in the Search view.
2. In the 'Find' field, enter the text to search for; in 'Replace' field, enter the replacement text.
3. Click 'Replace All' or use the Replace icons next to each result to selectively replace.
4. Use the .* (regex) button to enable regular expression mode if needed.
1. With your project folder open, go to File → Save Workspace As….
2. Choose a location and file name with the .code-workspace extension.
3. Click Save; a workspace file is created that references your folders and settings.
1. With a workspace open, go to File → Add Folder to Workspace….
2. Browse and select the folder you want to add, then click Add.
3. The new folder appears in the Explorer under the workspace; you can add multiple folders.
4. Save the workspace to persist changes.
1. Select the line or block of code you want to indent.
2. Press Tab to indent right or Shift+Tab to indent left (outdent).
3. To indent by a specific number of spaces, set 'Editor: Tab Size' in Settings.
4. For multiple lines, highlight them all before pressing Tab.
1. Download the .vsix extension file to your computer.
2. Open the Extensions view (Ctrl+Shift+X).
3. Click the three dots (More Actions) and select 'Install from VSIX...'.
4. Browse to the .vsix file and click Open.
5. VS Code installs the extension; reload if prompted.

thunderbird.name: Mozilla Thunderbird
general_tips: Account Settings can be accessed by right‑clicking on an account name in the folder pane and selecting 'Settings'.
The Address Book (Ctrl+Shift+B) manages contacts and mailing lists.
You can drag and drop messages into folders to organize them.
Use Add‑ons and Themes (Ctrl+Shift+A) to extend Thunderbird’s functionality.
Press F5 or click Get Messages to manually check for new mail.

steps: 1. Open Thunderbird.
2. Go to Account Settings (right‑click an account → Settings).
3. Click Account Actions → Add Mail Account.
4. Enter your name, email address and password.
5. Click Continue and let Thunderbird attempt to find server settings, then click Done.
1. Click the Write button in the toolbar or press Ctrl+N.
2. Enter the recipient’s email address in the To field, add a subject and compose your message.
3. Click Send to deliver the email.
4. Use Attach (paperclip icon) to add files to your email if needed.
1. Go to Account Settings for the desired account.
2. Under the account name, select 'Signature text' and type your desired signature, or choose 'Attach the signature from a file'.
3. Check 'Use HTML' if your signature contains formatting or images.
4. Click OK to save the signature.
1. Right‑click your account name or an existing folder in the folder pane.
2. Choose 'New Folder…'.
3. Enter a name for the folder and select its parent location.
4. Click Create Folder.
1. Go to Tools → Message Filters…
2. Click New to create a new filter.
3. Provide a filter name, choose the account and set matching criteria (e.g., From contains 'newsletter').
4. Add one or more actions (move to folder, tag, mark as read).
5. Click OK, then Run Now to apply the filter.
1. Create the target folder by right‑clicking the account and choosing New Folder…, entering a name such as 'Discounts'.
2. Go to Tools → Message Filters….
3. Click New and give the filter a name (e.g., Move Discount Emails).
4. Set the condition: Subject contains 'discount' (case‑insensitive).
5. Set the action: Move Message to the 'Discounts' folder.
6. Click OK and ensure the filter is enabled; click Run Now to process existing messages.
1. Click Write or press Ctrl+N to compose a new email.
2. Fill in the recipient, subject and message body.
3. Click the Attach button (paperclip icon) and select File….
4. Browse to the file (e.g., a PDF), select it and click Open.
5. The file appears in the Attachments pane; click Send when ready.
1. In Thunderbird, go to Account Settings → Account Actions → Add Mail Account.
2. Enter your name, Outlook email address and password, then click Continue.
3. Thunderbird attempts to automatically detect server settings; choose IMAP or POP and verify incoming/outgoing server details if necessary.
4. Click Done to create the account and Thunderbird will begin syncing messages.
5. If asked to sign in with modern authentication, follow the prompts from Outlook/Microsoft login pages.
1. Obtain the forwarding address you want to send messages to (e.g., your Gmail address).
2. Open Tools → Message Filters… and click New.
3. Name the filter (e.g., Forward to Gmail).
4. Set conditions (e.g., For all messages or specific criteria).
5. Under 'Perform these actions', choose 'Forward Message to' and enter the forwarding address.
6. Click OK and ensure the filter is active; messages matching the criteria will be forwarded automatically.

libreoffice_impress.name: LibreOffice Impress
general_tips: Use the left slide pane to navigate, reorder or duplicate slides by right‑clicking on a slide thumbnail.
Insert new slides via Slide → New Slide or press Ctrl+M.
Right‑click on objects to access context‑sensitive formatting options.
Save presentations frequently with Ctrl+S and enable auto‑save under Tools → Options → Load/Save.
Run your slide show via Slide Show → Start from First Slide or press F5.

steps: 1. Select the text box or highlight the text you want to change.
2. Go to Format → Character…
3. In the Font tab, select the desired font family (e.g., Times New Roman) and size.
4. Click OK to apply the changes.
1. Click into the text box and select the text whose color you want to change.
2. Go to Format → Character… and open the Font Effects tab.
3. Choose a color from the Font Color drop‑down menu (e.g., yellow, red, green).
4. Click OK to apply.
1. In the Slides pane, right‑click the slide you want to duplicate.
2. Choose 'Duplicate Slide'.
3. The duplicate appears after the selected slide; drag it to a new position if needed.
1. Click on the desired slide thumbnail in the left Slides pane to navigate to it.
2. Alternatively, press Page Up/Page Down to move to the previous or next slide.
3. Use the Navigator (F5) and choose Slide to jump directly to a particular slide by number.
1. Go to Insert → Image…
2. Browse and select the image file you want to add.
3. Click Open; the image appears on the current slide.
4. Drag the handles to resize or reposition the image.
1. Go to Format → Slide Properties…
2. In the Background tab, choose Color from the drop‑down menu.
3. Select the desired color or click More Colors for custom values.
4. Choose to apply the background to the selected slide or all slides and click OK.
1. Choose File → Export…
2. In the file type drop‑down, select an image format such as PNG or JPEG.
3. If you want only the current slide, tick 'Selection'; otherwise, all slides will export as separate images.
4. Set a filename and click Save.
1. Go to Slide → Properties… or Page Setup depending on your version.
2. In the Page tab, select either Landscape or Portrait orientation.
3. Click OK; all slides will adjust to the new orientation.
1. Open Tools → Options…
2. Navigate to Load/Save → General.
3. Check 'Save AutoRecovery information every' and set a time interval in minutes.
4. Click OK to enable automatic saving of your presentation.
1. Go to Insert → Slide Number… to enable slide numbers if they aren’t already shown.
2. Right‑click the slide number text box on the master slide (View → Master Slide) and choose Character…
3. In the Font Effects tab, choose a color (e.g., red, green, blue) for slide numbers.
4. Close the master view to return to your presentation.

system.name: Linux Terminal / System Administration
general_tips: Use 'man <command>' to read the manual page for any command.
Pipe output with '|' to chain commands (e.g., 'ls | grep txt').
Use 'sudo' for commands requiring root privileges.
Ctrl+C interrupts a running command; Ctrl+Z suspends it.
Use 'history' to view previous commands and '!n' to re-run command number n.

steps: 1. Open a terminal.
2. Run 'top -b -d 1 -n 5' to capture 5 snapshots of CPU usage at 1-second intervals in batch mode.
3. Redirect output to a file, e.g., 'top -b -d 1 -n 5 > /home/user/top_log.txt'.
4. Use 'less' or 'cat' to view the log file.
1. Navigate to the directory containing the symlink.
2. Run 'ls -l' to identify broken links (they appear red or with 'No such file').
3. Remove the broken link with 'rm <linkname>'.
4. Recreate the symlink with 'ln -s /path/to/target <linkname>'.
5. Verify with 'ls -l <linkname>'.
1. Use 'find /path -type f -printf "%s\t%p\n"' to list files with sizes.
2. Pipe to 'sort -nr' to sort by size descending.
3. Use 'head -n 5' to take the top 5 largest.
4. Optionally use 'numfmt --to=iec' to format sizes as human-readable.
5. Redirect to a file, e.g., '> top5.txt'.
1. Navigate to the directory containing the file.
2. Run 'sha256sum <filename>' to compute the checksum.
3. Compare the output with the expected checksum.
4. If checksums match, the file is verified; otherwise, it may be corrupted.
5. Use shell scripting to automate: 'if [ "$ACTUAL" = "$EXPECTED" ]; then ... fi'.

audacity.name: Audacity Audio Editor
general_tips: Use Ctrl+Shift+N to create a new stereo track.
Press R to start recording, Space to play/pause.
Ctrl+Z to undo, Ctrl+Shift+Z to redo.
Export via File → Export → Export as MP3/WAV.

steps: 1. Open GNOME Sound Recorder and record your audio clip, saving as .wav.
2. Open Audacity and go to File → Open to load the .wav file.
3. Select the portion of audio you want to trim (e.g., first 2 seconds of silence).
4. Press Delete to remove the selected portion.
5. Go to File → Export → Export as MP3.
6. Choose the destination path and click Save.
1. Open the audio file in Audacity.
2. Go to File → Export → Export as MP3.
3. Choose a filename and location.
4. Configure MP3 options (bitrate, quality) if needed.
5. Click Save to export.

typora.name: Typora Markdown Editor
general_tips: Typora renders Markdown in real-time as you type.
Use File → Export to convert to PDF, HTML, or other formats.
Ctrl+/ toggles source code view.

steps: 1. Open Typora and open the Markdown file (e.g., notes.md).
2. Go to File → Export → PDF.
3. Choose the destination path and filename.
4. Click Save to export the PDF.

pdfarranger.name: PDF Arranger
general_tips: Drag and drop PDF files into the window to add them.
Reorder pages by dragging thumbnails.
Use File → Save As to save the merged/arranged PDF.

steps: 1. Open PDF Arranger.
2. Click File → Open or drag the first PDF into the window.
3. Click File → Import or drag additional PDFs to add more pages.
4. Arrange pages by dragging thumbnails if needed.
5. Go to File → Save As and choose the output path.
6. Click Save to create the merged PDF.

gimagereader.name: gImageReader (OCR)
general_tips: gImageReader uses Tesseract OCR engine to extract text from images.
Supports PNG, JPEG, TIFF, and PDF input files.
Use Ctrl+O to add files for OCR processing.

steps: 1. Open gImageReader.
2. Press Ctrl+O or go to File → Open to add an image file (e.g., note.png).
3. Click the 'Recognize' button to run OCR.
4. Wait for the OCR process to complete.
5. Click 'Save' or go to File → Save Output to export the recognized text to a .txt file.
6. Optionally, open the text file in a text editor (e.g., Gedit) to verify.

gnome_calendar.name: GNOME Calendar
general_tips: Click the '+' button to create a new event.
Events can have reminders set for minutes/hours before.
GNOME Calendar syncs with online accounts configured in Settings.

steps: 1. Open GNOME Calendar.
2. Click the '+' (New Event) button.
3. Enter the event title (e.g., 'Team Sync Meeting').
4. Set the date and time (e.g., next Friday at 14:00).
5. Click 'Add Reminder' and select a reminder time (e.g., 10 minutes before).
6. Click Save to create the event.
7. A desktop notification will appear at the reminder time.

terminal.name: GNOME Terminal
general_tips: Use Ctrl+Alt+T to open a new terminal window.
Terminal preferences are accessed via the hamburger menu (☰) → Preferences.
Profile settings control default terminal size, colors, and fonts.
In preferences dialogs, numeric fields are spin-button elements showing their current value (e.g., '80', '24').

steps: 1. Open Terminal using HOTKEY [ctrl, alt, t].
2. Click the hamburger Menu button (☰) in the title bar.
3. Click 'Preferences' in the dropdown menu.
4. Click on the profile name (e.g., 'Unnamed') in the sidebar.
5. The 'Text' tab shows 'Initial terminal size' with columns and rows.
6. IMPORTANT: To edit the size, click on the spin-button showing the current value (e.g., click on '80' to change columns).
7. Use TRIPLE_CLICK or Ctrl+A to select all text, then TYPE the new value.
8. Similarly edit the rows field by clicking on '24' and typing the new value.
9. Close the preferences window - changes are saved automatically.

element_hints.columns_field: Look for spin-button element with value '80'
element_hints.rows_field: Look for spin-button element with value '24'

steps: 1. Open Terminal preferences via Menu → Preferences.
2. Select your profile in the sidebar.
3. Click the 'Colors' tab.
4. Uncheck 'Use colors from system theme' to customize.
5. Choose a built-in scheme or set custom colors.
6. Close the dialog to save changes.
